items.title: Introduction to the Sangam Age
items.body:
## What Was the Sangam Age?

- The **Sangam Age** refers to the period **c. 300 BCE – 300 CE** in South India, marked by the flowering of **Tamil literature** and vibrant political, economic and social life.
- The word **'Sangam'** means an **assembly / gathering of poets and scholars** working under **royal patronage**.
- **Three Sangams (Muchchangam)** are believed to have been held to promote the **Tamil language and literature**.
- The land of the Tamils was called **Tamilakam**, ruled by three crowned dynasties — the **Cheras, Cholas and Pandyas (the Muvendar)** — alongside minor chieftains (Velir).
- **Primary sources:** Sangam literature (Tolkappiyam, Ettuthokai, Pattuppattu), the epics **Silappathikaram** and **Manimekalai**, plus archaeological remains such as Roman coins.

figure.alt: Timeline of the early history of South India showing megalithic burials and the Sangam Age (3rd century BCE to 3rd century CE) ending with the Kalabhra takeover
figure.caption: The Sangam Age (c. 3rd century BCE – 3rd century CE) in the early history of South India, closing with the Kalabhra takeover.

keyPoints: Sangam Age: c. 300 BCE – 300 CE in South India (Tamilakam).
'Sangam' = assembly of poets/scholars under royal patronage.
Three Sangams (Muchchangam) promoted Tamil language and literature.
Ruled by three crowned kings — Cheras, Cholas, Pandyas (Muvendar).
Sources: Sangam literature, epics (Silappathikaram, Manimekalai), Roman coins.
items.mnemonic: Sangam = Assembly; three crowned kings of Tamilakam = 'Cheras, Cholas, Pandyas' (Muvendar).
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: Sangam Age (Introduction to the Sangam Age)

items.title: The Three Sangam Assemblies (Muchchangam)
items.body:
## Three Sangams

- **First Sangam** — held at **Madurai**, presided over by the sage **Agastya (Agattiyar)**; no work survives (the *Agayattiyam* is traditionally attributed to it). Said to be attended by gods, sages and legendary figures.
- **Second Sangam** — held at **Kapadapuram**, presided over by **Tolkappiyar**; its only surviving work is the **Tolkappiyam**, the earliest Tamil grammar. It laid down the rules of Tamil grammar.
- **Third Sangam** — held again at **Madurai**, presided over by **Nakkirar**; it produced the **Ettuthokai (Eight Anthologies)** and **Pattuppattu (Ten Idylls)**, and was attended by numerous poets including **Avvaiyar**.
- **Madurai** hosted both the First and Third Sangams, making it the great literary capital of the Tamils.
keyPoints: First Sangam: Madurai, presided by Agastya; no surviving work.
Second Sangam: Kapadapuram, presided by Tolkappiyar; Tolkappiyam survives.
Third Sangam: Madurai, presided by Nakkirar; Ettuthokai + Pattuppattu.
Avvaiyar was a celebrated poet of the Third Sangam.
Madurai hosted the First and Third Sangams.
items.mnemonic: First & Third at Madurai (Agastya, Nakkirar); Second at Kapadapuram (Tolkappiyar → Tolkappiyam).
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: Sangam Age (Sangam Assemblies – Muchchangam)

items.title: The Three Crowned Kings — Emblems, Capitals & Ports
items.body:
## The Muvendar (Three Crowned Kings)

The **Cheras, Cholas and Pandyas** formed the **Muvendar** and controlled distinct regions of Tamilakam.

| Dynasty | Emblem | Capital | Chief Port |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Chera** | Bow (Villavar) | **Vanji (Karur)** | **Muziris** (also Tondi) |
| **Chola** | Tiger | **Uraiyur** | **Puhar / Kaviripattinam** |
| **Pandya** | Fish | **Madurai** | **Korkai** |

- The **Cheras** ruled modern **Kerala and western Tamil Nadu**; their bow emblem echoes their title **Villavar** (bowmen).
- The **Cholas** held the **Cauvery delta**, extending to parts of **southern Andhra Pradesh** (between the Pennar and Vellar rivers).
- The **Pandyas** ruled **southern Tamil Nadu** from Madurai on the Vaigai, famed for **pearl fishing at Korkai**.

figure.alt: Map of the Sangam Age showing the Chera, Chola and Pandya territories with Karur, Uraiyur, Thanjavur and Madurai marked
figure.caption: The three crowned kingdoms of the Sangam Age — Chera (Karur), Chola (Uraiyur) and Pandya (Madurai).

keyPoints: Chera: emblem bow, capital Vanji (Karur), port Muziris.
Chola: emblem tiger, capital Uraiyur, port Puhar (Kaviripattinam).
Pandya: emblem fish, capital Madurai, port Korkai.
Chola territory reached parts of southern Andhra Pradesh (Pennar–Vellar).
Together the three formed the Muvendar (three crowned kings).
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: Sangam Age (Kingdoms During the Sangam Age)

items.title: The Chola Dynasty
items.body:
## The Cholas of the Sangam Age

- **Capitals:** **Uraiyur** (famous for its cotton trade) and the port city **Kaveripattinam (Puhar)**, a hub of maritime trade.
- **Emblem:** the **Tiger**.
- **Territory:** from the **Cauvery delta** in modern Tamil Nadu to parts of **southern Andhra Pradesh**, between the **Pennar and Vellar rivers**.
- **Royal titles:** **Senni, Valavan and Killi**, reflecting valour and tradition.
- **Elara**, an early Chola king, is remembered in the **Mahavamsa** for his just rule in **Sri Lanka** until he was defeated by the Sinhalese prince **Dutugemunu**.
- The greatest Sangam Chola was **Karikala** (see separate note).
keyPoints: Capitals: Uraiyur (cotton trade) and Kaveripattinam/Puhar (port).
Emblem: tiger; titles Senni, Valavan, Killi.
Territory reached from the Cauvery delta to southern Andhra Pradesh.
Elara ruled justly in Sri Lanka (Mahavamsa); defeated by Dutugemunu.
Karikala was the greatest Sangam Chola ruler.
items.mnemonic: Chola = Tiger; Uraiyur (cotton) + Puhar (port); titles Senni-Valavan-Killi.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: Sangam Age (Chola Dynasty)

items.title: Karikala Chola — Kallanai & the Grand Anicut
items.body:
## Karikala Chola

- Rose to power despite **internal family conflicts** over succession.
- **Battle of Venni:** defeated a confederacy of the **Chera, Pandya and 11 minor chieftains**, consolidating Chola supremacy.
- **Battle of Vahaipparandalai:** defeated **nine chieftains**, further strengthening his hold over the Tamil region.
- **Greatest contribution:** built the **Kallanai Dam (Grand Anicut)** across the **Cauvery River** — one of the **oldest dams in the world still in use** — along with irrigation tanks and canals.
- Under him the port of **Puhar (Kaveripattinam)** became a centre of foreign trade, drawing **Roman and Greek merchants** who brought gold, wine and horses.
keyPoints: Won the Battle of Venni against a Chera–Pandya + 11-chieftain confederacy.
Won the Battle of Vahaipparandalai over nine chieftains.
Built the Kallanai Dam (Grand Anicut) across the Cauvery — among the world's oldest dams still in use.
Promoted irrigation tanks and canals for agriculture.
Made Puhar a hub of Roman and Greek maritime trade.
items.mnemonic: Karikala = 'Kallanai (Grand Anicut) on the Cauvery' + victories at Venni & Vahaipparandalai.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: Sangam Age (Karikala Chola)

items.title: The Chera Dynasty
items.body:
## The Cheras of the Sangam Age

- **Capital:** **Vanji (Karur)**, the political centre; major ports **Muziris** and **Tondi** handled **Roman trade**.
- **Emblem:** the **Bow**.
- **Territory:** modern-day **Kerala and western Tamil Nadu**.
- **Titles:** **Vanavaramban, Kuttuvan, Irumporai and Villavar**.
- **Perumchotru Udhiyan Cheralathan** was famed for generosity — legend says he fed **both armies during the Mahabharata war**.
- **Imayavaramban Nedum Cheralathan** led a **Himalayan expedition** (northern expansion), recorded in the Sangam work **Pathitrupathu (Pathitrupattu)**.
keyPoints: Capital Vanji (Karur); ports Muziris and Tondi for Roman trade.
Emblem: bow; ruled Kerala and western Tamil Nadu.
Titles: Vanavaramban, Kuttuvan, Irumporai, Villavar.
Udhiyan Cheralathan fed both armies in the Mahabharata war (generosity).
Imayavaramban Nedum Cheralathan's Himalayan expedition (recorded in Pathitrupathu).
items.mnemonic: Chera = Bow; Vanji (Karur) + ports Muziris/Tondi; 'Imayavaramban went to the Himalayas'.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: Sangam Age (Chera Dynasty)

items.title: Cheran Senguttuvan & the Gajabahu Synchronism
items.body:
## Cheran Senguttuvan

- The most celebrated Chera ruler; led an **expedition to the Himalayas**, defeating several northern monarchs. His deeds are recorded in the epic **Silappathikaram**.
- Founded the **Pattini Cult**, worshipping **Kannagi** — the heroine of Silappathikaram — as the **goddess of chastity**.
- **Gajabahu Synchronism:** Senguttuvan was a contemporary of the **Sri Lankan king Gajabahu (II)**, who is said to have attended the consecration of the Kannagi/Pattini temple. This synchronism is a key **anchor for dating the Sangam Age** and shows the close ties between South India and Sri Lanka.
keyPoints: Greatest Chera ruler; Himalayan expedition recorded in Silappathikaram.
Founded the Pattini Cult worshipping Kannagi as goddess of chastity.
Contemporary of Sri Lankan king Gajabahu (Gajabahu synchronism).
The Gajabahu synchronism is a key chronological anchor for the Sangam Age.
Shows close India–Sri Lanka links in this period.
items.mnemonic: Senguttuvan = Pattini Cult (Kannagi) + Gajabahu synchronism (the dating anchor).
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: Sangam Age (Cheran Senguttuvan)

items.title: The Pandya Dynasty
items.body:
## The Pandyas of the Sangam Age

- **Capital:** **Madurai**, on the banks of the **Vaigai River** — the political and cultural hub; the port **Korkai** was famed for **pearl fishing**.
- **Emblem:** the **Fish**.
- **Territory:** southern Tamil Nadu, with close trade ties to the **Romans** (Roman emissaries visited).
- **Titles:** **Thennavar** (Southern King) and **Minavar** (Warrior of the Seas).
- **Aryappadai Kadantha Neduncheliyan** defeated Aryan forces and ordered the execution of **Kovalan** (Silappathikaram), leading Kannagi to burn Madurai.
- **Thalaiyalanganaattu Cheruvendra Neduncheliyan** defeated a Chera–Chola–Velir coalition at the **Battle of Thalaiyalanganam**. **Uggira Peruvaludhi** was the last Sangam Pandya, before the **Kalabhra** invasion.
keyPoints: Capital Madurai (on the Vaigai); port Korkai famed for pearl fishing.
Emblem: fish; titles Thennavar and Minavar.
Neduncheliyan (Aryappadai Kadantha) ordered Kovalan's execution → burning of Madurai.
Battle of Thalaiyalanganam won by Thalaiyalanganaattu Neduncheliyan.
Uggira Peruvaludhi was the last Sangam Pandya before the Kalabhra invasion.
items.mnemonic: Pandya = Fish; Madurai (Vaigai) + Korkai (pearls); titles Thennavar/Minavar.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: Sangam Age (Pandya Dynasty)

items.title: Sangam Literature — Grammar, Anthologies & Tirukkural
items.body:
## The Body of Sangam Literature

- **Tolkappiyam** (by **Tolkappiyar**) — the **earliest Tamil grammar**; besides grammar it describes the political, social and economic conditions of the age.
- **Ettuthokai (Eight Anthologies)** — narrative poems by poets such as Kapilar, Nakkirar and Avvaiyar, praising love, heroism and the valour of kings.
- **Pattuppattu (Ten Idylls / Ten Long Poems)** — by multiple poets, on heroic deeds, kingship and Sangam society.
- **Pathinenkilkanakku (Eighteen Lesser Works)** — didactic/moral texts; the most famous is the **Tirukkural**.
- **Tirukkural** (by **Thiruvalluvar**) — **1,330 couplets** in three sections: **Virtue (Aram), Wealth (Porul) and Love (Inbam)** — a revered ethical classic.
keyPoints: Tolkappiyam = earliest Tamil grammar (author Tolkappiyar).
Ettuthokai = Eight Anthologies; Pattuppattu = Ten Idylls.
Pathinenkilkanakku = Eighteen Lesser (didactic) Works.
Tirukkural by Thiruvalluvar: 1,330 couplets in Virtue, Wealth, Love.
Sangam texts also reveal political, social and economic life.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: Sangam Age (Sangam Literature)

items.title: The Twin Epics — Silappathikaram & Manimekalai
items.body:
## The Two Great Tamil Epics

- **Silappathikaram** (by **Ilango Adigal**) — depicts the devotion of **Kannagi** to her husband **Kovalan**; explores love, betrayal and justice, and richly reflects Sangam society, culture and polity. Kannagi's story underlies the **Pattini Cult**.
- **Manimekalai** (by **Sittalai Sattanar**) — a **Buddhist epic** about **Manimekalai**, the daughter of **Kovalan and Madhavi**; it explores spirituality and dharma, tracing her transformation into a **Buddhist nun** and emphasising Nirvana.
- Together the two epics are the **twin epics of Tamil literature**, offering vivid pictures of ethics, religion and social life of the age.
keyPoints: Silappathikaram by Ilango Adigal — Kannagi's devotion to Kovalan.
Manimekalai by Sittalai Sattanar — a Buddhist epic.
Manimekalai = daughter of Kovalan and Madhavi; becomes a nun.
Silappathikaram inspired the Pattini Cult of Kannagi.
The two are the twin epics of Tamil literature.
items.mnemonic: Silappathikaram (Ilango Adigal → Kannagi–Kovalan); Manimekalai (Sattanar → Buddhist, their daughter).
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: Sangam Age (Sangam Literature – Epics)

items.title: Sangam Society & the Tinai (Five Landscapes)
items.body:
## The Five-fold Land Division (Aintinai)

The **Tolkappiyam** describes a **five-fold land division (Panchitanai / Tinai)**, each with its own deity and way of life:

| Landscape | Deity | Occupation |
|---|---|---|
| **Kurinji** (hills) | Murugan | Hunting, honey collection |
| **Mullai** (pastoral) | Vishnu (Mayon) | Cattle rearing |
| **Marudam** (agricultural) | Indra | Agriculture |
| **Neydal** (coastal) | Varuna | Fishing, salt production |
| **Palai** (desert) | Korravai | Robbery / raiding |

- Society also had four broad groups: **Arasar** (ruling class), **Anthanar** (priests), **Vanigar** (traders) and **Vellalar** (agriculturists).
- **Women** enjoyed relative freedom — choosing partners, and contributing to literature (poets **Avvaiyar, Nachchellaiyar, Kakkaipadiniyar**); yet **Karpu (chastity)** was idealised and **Sati** occurred among some aristocratic families.
keyPoints: Tolkappiyam's five landscapes: Kurinji, Mullai, Marudam, Neydal, Palai.
Deities: Murugan, Vishnu, Indra, Varuna, Korravai respectively.
Social groups: Arasar, Anthanar, Vanigar, Vellalar.
Women had relative freedom; poets Avvaiyar, Nachchellaiyar, Kakkaipadiniyar.
Karpu (chastity) idealised; Sati among some aristocratic families.
items.mnemonic: Tinai (KMMNP): Kurinji-Mullai-Marudam-Neydal-Palai → hills, pasture, farms, coast, desert.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: Sangam Age (Sangam Society; Position of Women)

items.title: Sangam Economy & Indo-Roman Trade
items.body:
## Economy of the Sangam Age

- **Agriculture** was the backbone: **rice** (staple), sugarcane, cotton, pepper, turmeric, ginger and jackfruit; irrigation tanks, wells and the **Kallanai Dam** (Karikala) boosted output.
- **Handicrafts:** weaving (Uraiyur cotton prized in Roman markets), metalwork, shipbuilding; craft centres included **Arikamedu** (beads/ceramics), Madurai and Kanchipuram.
- **Internal trade** ran on a **barter system**; **Umanar** (salt merchants) and mobile traders (**Chattu**) moved goods; **Vanikan** = merchant.
- **External trade** linked Tamil ports — **Puhar, Musiri (Muziris), Korkai, Arikamedu, Tondi** — with **Rome, Greece and Southeast Asia**.
- **Exports:** spices (pepper, turmeric, cardamom), textiles, pearls, ivory; **Imports:** gold, Roman wine, horses.
- **Roman coins** (gold and silver) found across Tamil Nadu confirm robust Indo-Roman trade; they were used both as currency and as ornaments.

figure.alt: Three Roman gold coins found in Tamil Nadu, sometimes worn as jewellery
figure.caption: Roman coins unearthed in Tamil Nadu — evidence of flourishing Indo-Roman trade; sometimes worn as jewellery.

keyPoints: Agriculture the backbone; Kallanai Dam aided irrigation.
Uraiyur cotton prized in Rome; Arikamedu a key craft/trade centre.
Internal trade by barter; Umanar = salt merchants, Vanikan = merchant.
Ports Puhar, Muziris, Korkai, Arikamedu, Tondi traded with Rome/Greece.
Exports: spices, textiles, pearls, ivory; Imports: gold, wine, horses.
Roman coins in Tamil Nadu prove Indo-Roman trade.
items.mnemonic: Export spices/pearls/textiles → Import gold/wine/horses; proof = Roman coins.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: Sangam Age (Sangam Economy; External Trade; Roman Coins)

items.title: Sangam Polity & Administration
items.body:
## Government & Administration

- **Hereditary monarchy** was the norm; kings took grand titles such as **Thennavar** (Southern King) and **Minavar** (Warrior of the Seas).
- **Advisory officials:** **Amaichar** (ministers), **Anthanar** (priests), **Senathipathi** (military commanders), **Otrar** (spies) and **Thuthar** (envoys).
- **Administrative divisions:** **Mandalam** (province) → **Nadu** (district) → **Ur** (town) → **Perur** (large village) → **Sirur** (small village). Coastal trade towns were **Pattinam**; suburbs of artisans were **Cheri**.
- **Revenue:** **Karai** (land tax), **Ulgu** (customs duty), **Irai** (tribute) and **Iravu** (extra demand); plus **war booty**.
- Each king kept a **standing army** with distinctive war banners (**Kodimaram**).
keyPoints: Hereditary monarchy; titles Thennavar and Minavar.
Officials: Amaichar, Anthanar, Senathipathi, Otrar, Thuthar.
Divisions: Mandalam > Nadu > Ur > Perur > Sirur; Pattinam (ports), Cheri (suburbs).
Revenue: Karai (land tax), Ulgu (customs), Irai (tribute), Iravu (extra demand).
Standing armies with Kodimaram (war banners); war booty a source of income.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: Sangam Age (Sangam Polity and Administration)

items.title: Sangam Religion & the Kalabhra Decline
items.body:
## Religion & the End of the Age

- **Murugan (Seyon)** was the chief deity — god of war, valour and youth — with six abodes (**Arupadai Veedu**), worshipped especially in the hilly **Kurinji** country.
- Other deities: **Vishnu (Mayon)** (guardian, agricultural areas), **Indra** (rain/thunder), **Varuna** (seas/coast), and **Korravai** (goddess of war and victory).
- **Hero stones (Nadu Kal)** were raised for warriors fallen in battle or cattle raids — a form of ancestor and valour worship.
- **Decline:** the **Kalabhras**, a tribal dynasty, invaded Tamil Nadu around the **3rd century CE** and ruled for over **250 years**, displacing the Cheras, Cholas and Pandyas — often called the **'dark age'**. **Buddhism and Jainism** gained prominence, yet literature (e.g. the Tirukkural) thrived. The **Pallavas and Pandyas** re-established power by the **6th century CE**.
keyPoints: Chief deity Murugan (Seyon), with six abodes (Arupadai Veedu).
Other gods: Vishnu/Mayon, Indra, Varuna, Korravai.
Hero stones (Nadu Kal) honoured fallen warriors.
Kalabhras invaded (~3rd century CE), ruled 250+ years — the 'dark age'.
Buddhism/Jainism rose; Pallavas & Pandyas revived power by 6th century CE.
items.mnemonic: Gods: Murugan first (Kurinji); End = Kalabhra 'dark age' → revived by Pallavas & Pandyas.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: Sangam Age (Sangam Religion; Decline of the Sangam Age)

items.title: Sangam Archaeology — Keeladi, Arikamedu, Adichanallur (PYQ & CA)
items.body:
## Digging up the Sangam Age

| Site | River / location | Significance |
|---|---|---|
| **Keeladi (Keezhadi)** | Vaigai, near Madurai (TN) | ASI/TN excavations revealed a **literate, urban Sangam-era settlement**; **Tamil-Brahmi** graffiti/potsherds; carbon dates pushed Tamil urbanism back to **c. 6th century BCE**. A major **2025–26 current-affairs** flashpoint (ASI report controversy). |
| **Arikamedu** | Coast near Puducherry | **Indo-Roman trade emporium** — Roman pottery (Arretine ware), amphorae, beads. |
| **Adichanallur** | Thamirabarani (TN) | Iron Age–megalithic **urn burials**, skeletal remains, bronze/iron objects. |

- **Keeladi** is the highest-yield new fact: it provides **material proof** of the Sangam texts' picture of urban, literate Tamil society and is repeatedly cited in 2025–26 CA quizzes.
- **Discrimination point:** the tank-land grant terms **'Eripatti' (tank land)** and elaborate land-grant records belong to the **later Imperial Cholas (9th–13th c. CE)**, NOT the Sangam-age Cholas — a classic trap.
keyPoints: Keeladi (Keezhadi), on the Vaigai near Madurai, revealed a literate urban Sangam settlement with Tamil-Brahmi graffiti; dates pushed back to c. 6th century BCE.
Keeladi is a major 2025–26 current-affairs topic (ASI report controversy).
Arikamedu (near Puducherry) = Indo-Roman trade emporium with Arretine ware and amphorae.
Adichanallur (Thamirabarani) = Iron Age megalithic urn-burial site.
'Eripatti' (tank land) and formal land grants belong to the later Imperial Cholas, NOT the Sangam Cholas.
items.source: ASI / Tamil Nadu State Department of Archaeology reports on Keeladi; standard facts on Arikamedu and Adichanallur
